# YFL Expense Tracker

Family expense tracking app built with SvelteKit 2, Svelte 5, Supabase, and Tailwind CSS 4.

## Commands

```bash
npm run dev          # Dev server on localhost:5173
npm run build        # Production build
npm run check        # Type checking (svelte-check)
npm run test:unit    # Vitest unit tests
npm run test:e2e     # Playwright e2e tests
npm test             # Full test suite (unit + e2e)
npm run lint         # Prettier check + ESLint
npm run format       # Auto-format with Prettier
```

## Architecture

- **Routes:** `src/routes/` — SvelteKit file-based routing
- **Services:** `src/lib/services/` — Business logic (ExpenseService, ReceiptService, etc.). Some use DI (take Supabase client as param), others use singleton pattern with module-level import.
- **Models:** `src/lib/models/` — TypeScript data models
- **Components:** `src/lib/components/` — Reusable Svelte components
- **Utils:** `src/lib/utils/` — Helper functions with co-located `.spec.ts` tests
- **Server:** `src/lib/server/` — Server-only code (file validation, OCR processing)
- **CSV Parsers:** `src/lib/services/csvParsers/` — Bank-specific CSV parsers (Amex, PC Financial, RBC, TD, Simplii, EQ Bank, Wealth Simple) with `BaseCSVParser` and `CSVParserFactory` for auto-detection
- **Docs:** `docs/` — Project documentation. `docs/adr/` (architecture decision records), `docs/plans/` (design docs — **when the work is done, `git mv` the plan to `docs/plans-done/`**, same reason and same depth as `prd-done/`, so its `../` links keep working; fix inbound links), `docs/prd-*.md` (active PRDs — in-file `**Status:**` front-matter carries the detail; **when a PRD is finished, `git mv` it to `docs/prd-done/`** so done-vs-active is visible from `ls` without opening files, and fix its now-one-level-deeper relative links plus any inbound links), `docs/product-backlog.md` (the single working list — features, bugs, engineering, and open refactoring items as one-liners) plus `docs/refactoring-backlog.md` (detailed RF-NN reference, not a separate to-do list), `docs/domain-model.md` (ubiquitous-language glossary). Prefer `docs/` over root for any new note or plan; the root keeps only `README.md` and `CLAUDE.md`.
- **Migrations:** `supabase/migrations/` — SQL migrations (schema + RLS policies)

## Supabase Migrations

Migrations live in `supabase/migrations/` as numbered SQL files. The project is linked to the remote Supabase project (`YFL Expense Tracker`, region `ca-central-1`).

```bash
supabase migration list           # Show local vs remote migration status
supabase db push                  # Push pending migrations to remote database
supabase db push --dry-run        # Preview what would be applied without running
supabase migration new <name>     # Create a new empty migration file
supabase db diff --schema public  # Generate migration from local schema changes
supabase db reset                 # Reset local DB and re-run all migrations (destructive)
```

**Naming convention:** `YYYYMMDD_description.sql` (e.g. `20260225_secure_receipts_storage.sql`).

**Squashed to a baseline (2026-07-26).** `supabase/migrations/` holds one file,
`20260726120000_baseline.sql`; the 31 predecessors are in `supabase/migrations-archive/`. They
could not rebuild the DB from scratch — replay died at `007` with `relation "public.families" does
not exist` because `families` was created by hand in the dashboard and only captured later by the
`20251010000319_remote_schema.sql` dump, which sorts _after_ `007`. Prod history was repaired to
match (bookkeeping only). **The baseline's storage section is hand-maintained** — `supabase db
dump` does not cover the `storage` schema, so the `receipts` bucket + its 4 policies are appended
manually at the end of the file. Any storage change must be reflected there too. Verify every new
migration with `npm run db:reset` before pushing. See `docs/local-dev.md`.

**Important:** The migration role does NOT own `storage.objects`, so `COMMENT ON POLICY` and `ALTER TABLE` on storage tables will fail. Stick to `CREATE POLICY` / `DROP POLICY` / `UPDATE storage.buckets` for storage changes.

## Key Patterns

- **Expenses are computed, not stored.** No "expenses" table — expenses are joins of receipts + expense_categories + categories. Each receipt maps to exactly one expense (1:1).
- **All data is family-scoped.** Users belong to families via `family_members`. RLS policies enforce family-level access on receipts, transactions, categories, and vendor rules.
- **Receipt storage is private.** The `receipts` bucket is private — all file access uses signed URLs via `getSignedReceiptUrl()` from `src/lib/utils/signedUrl.ts`. Pages cache signed URLs in a reactive `signedUrls` map loaded via `$effect`. OCR uses short-lived signed URLs (5 min expiry). Display uses 1-hour expiry.
- **Storage RLS is family-scoped for reads.** Family members can read each other's receipt files. Write/delete is restricted to the file owner (path prefix = `user_id`).
- **Auto-categorization:** Vendor rules map normalized merchant names to categories. Applied on page load for uncategorized expenses. Normalization: lowercase, strip special chars, trim.
- **Date pickers use flowbite-svelte.** Always use `<Datepicker>` from `flowbite-svelte` with `toDate()` and `toISODateString()` helpers from `$lib/utils/dateConversion`. Never use raw `<input type="date">`.
- **Never use `new Date("YYYY-MM-DD")` for date-only strings.** JavaScript parses bare date strings as UTC midnight, which shifts to the previous day in timezones west of UTC. Always use `toDate()` to parse or `formatDate()` to display — both from `$lib/utils/dateConversion`. These parse year/month/day parts manually to construct local-time Date objects.
- **Date filters preserved in URL** via `preserveFilters()` helper in `+layout.svelte`.
- **The quality gate is `vercel.json`, not GitHub Actions.** Vercel deploys by watching GitHub, and `buildCommand` runs `check` → `lint` → `vitest run --project server` → `build`, so a type error or lint failure means the build fails and **no deployment is created**. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is **advisory only** — it runs the `client` (browser/Chromium) Vitest project, which Vercel's build image can't, and gates nothing. Adding a check to the workflow does _not_ make it block a deploy; add it to `buildCommand`. This project never uses pull requests, and Vercel Deployment Checks were rejected deliberately — see [ADR 0005](docs/adr/0005-quality-gate-in-the-vercel-build-not-github-actions.md).
- **Version tracking** in `src/lib/version.ts`. Increment by 0.01 for small changes, 0.1 for features — but **only bump the version when the change is actually committed and pushed live.** Leave `version.ts` (and any version tag in the docs) untouched for uncommitted, in-progress work; the human assigns the number at commit time. Don't write a specific version tag (e.g. "v0.70") in design docs / the backlog for unreleased work — use "(pending release)" instead.
- **Transaction amounts: negative = expense, positive = refund/credit.** This matches the UI display (red = negative = expense, green = positive = credit). Most banks (PC Financial, EQ Bank, RBC, TD, Simplii) already use negative for expenses so parsers keep signs as-is (`invertSign: false`). Only American Express uses positive for expenses and needs `invertSign: true`. Wealth Simple CSV exports have inconsistent signs across downloads, so the parser uses the `type` column (Purchase → negative, Payment/Refund → positive) instead of `invertSign`. See `BaseCSVParser.normalizeAmount()`.
- **XLS/XLSX import supported.** Excel files are converted to CSV via `ExcelToCSVConverter` (SheetJS) before passing through the same parser pipeline. File type detected by extension/MIME.

## Gotchas

- Dual test environments: browser tests use Playwright provider, server tests use Node.js — configured in `vite.config.ts` under `test.projects`
- PDFs go directly to Mistral Vision API (pixtral-12b) — no conversion needed
- Suspicious date flag triggers for receipts >42 days old or future-dated
- Multi-email support: primary email in `auth.users`, up to 5 additional in `profiles` table. Email receipt ingestion checks both.
- File uploads: JPEG/PNG/HEIC up to 5MB, PDF up to 10MB. Validated client-side and server-side (`src/lib/server/fileValidation.ts`)
- Recent migrations (Jan–Feb 2026) refactored family-scoping, fixed RLS recursion issues, and secured storage — be careful modifying RLS policies
- Receipt image URLs are async (signed URLs). Components use `$effect` + `Promise.then()` to load them, not synchronous calls. Never use `getPublicUrl()`.
- Transaction imports accept CSV, XLS, and XLSX files. Excel files are read as ArrayBuffer and converted to CSV text before parsing.
- The `transactions` table uses `excluded` (boolean) for soft-delete. The UI shows "Exclude/Include" buttons. The database column was originally named `ignored` in older code paths.
- Debugging Resend (email receipts): start at <https://resend.com/webhooks> — it shows the endpoint **Signing Secret** (`whsec_…`, must equal Supabase's `RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET`) and the delivery log with the status our `resend` function returned. The webhook fails closed: `401` = signature mismatch, `500` = secret not configured. See `docs/email-notifications.md`.
- Image resize before upload: client-side, native Canvas (zero deps), 2000px longest axis, 85% quality, JPEG/PNG only (skips PDF + HEIC), falls back to the original file on any failure. Wired in `ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate()`; logic in `src/lib/utils/imageResize.ts`.
- On Supabase, `REVOKE … FROM PUBLIC` does **not** remove `anon` / `authenticated` — those roles hold _direct_ grants via default privileges, so revoke each role explicitly. A function can look locked down and still be anon-executable.
- PostgREST caps every query at **1000 rows by default**, silently. Any list that can exceed that must page in `.range()` batches until a short page (see `ExpenseService.getExpenses`), and any count must use an exact `head` count rather than a plain select's `.length`.
- Regenerating `.svelte-kit` does **not** update the root `tsconfig.json` `include`. The root config restates the generated list plus `scripts/**/*.ts` and `e2e/**/*.ts` (it replaces rather than merges), so `npm run check` covers them; if SvelteKit ever adds an entry, copy it across by hand. `supabase/functions/` stays out of scope (Deno — verify with `deno check`).
- `.env` is a **FIFO**, so nothing can read it twice. `npm run dev` works only because `op run --env-file=.env` consumes the named pipe and injects the values; a bare `vite build`, a second reader, or any tool expecting a regular file gets nothing. This is why `playwright.config.ts` hard-codes fake public config and the local scripts inline Supabase's well-known local defaults.
- Test harness: `src/lib/tests/harness/appMocks.ts` (+ `LayoutHarness.svelte`) mocks the SvelteKit + Supabase boundaries so real `+page.svelte` / `+layout.svelte` render in the `client` project (`setRoute`/`setSession`/`setReceipts`/… plus service stubs). The canonical chainable Supabase mock is `src/lib/tests/fixtures/supabaseMock.ts`; row builders in `rowBuilders.ts`; fetch stubs in `fixtures/fetchMock.ts`. Prefer these over a local copy — and when auditing for tests that reimplement production logic, look for logic inlined _inside_ `it()` bodies, not just `function`-defined helpers.
- `overflow-x-auto` clips dropdowns in BOTH axes: a wrapper whose `overflow-x` is non-visible has its computed `overflow-y` become `auto` (not `visible`), so `overflow-x-auto` on a table wrapper clips absolutely-positioned dropdown menus vertically too. Keep the expenses table wrapper free of it; position menus with `right-0`.
- Date-parsing correction vs flag windows: OCR date correction uses a 90-day window (`PLAUSIBILITY_WINDOW_DAYS`) while the suspicious-date FLAG uses 42 days — a 43–90-day date can be auto-accepted by the parser yet still flagged. Two failure modes: format-ambiguity (auto-fixable) vs wrong-token extraction (only flaggable). Ruled out — do not reintroduce: prompt-tuning date interpretation, using the matched bank-transaction date as truth (circular), extracting all date tokens. `raw_date_text` is transient (never persisted); the `supabase/functions/_shared/` Deno copy of the correction logic must stay in lock-step with `src/lib/utils/`.
- Password policy: 16-char minimum (NIST length-over-complexity), at least one of upper/lower/number/special, exact confirmation match (whitespace-preserving, case-sensitive). Constants/messages exported from `src/lib/utils/passwordValidation.ts`.

## Environment Variables

Public (browser): `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`
Private (server): `MISTRAL_API_KEY`, `RESEND_API_KEY`, `RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `RESEND_FROM_EMAIL` (sender for notification emails — MUST be an address on a domain verified in Resend, or every send returns 403 "Request is forbidden"; consumed by `supabase/functions/_shared/notify.ts`)

## Code Style

- Prettier: tabs, single quotes, no trailing commas, 100-char width
- ESLint flat config (v9) with TypeScript + Svelte plugins
- Svelte 5 rune syntax ($state, $derived, etc.)
- **Unused parameters and boolean flag arguments are only acceptable when an external API we don't control dictates the signature.** A parameter the body never reads, or a `boolean` that toggles between two behaviours, is allowed _only_ when it's forced on us by a callback/method we don't own — e.g. the unread `event` in Supabase's `onAuthStateChange((event, session) => …)`, or a third-party function that takes a boolean flag. In those cases prefix an unused param with `_` (`_event`). In our own code: drop unused parameters, and don't design boolean flag parameters — split the function in two or take an options object (see RF-11). `no-unused-vars` runs at its default (no `_` ignore pattern), so it flags unused vars and trailing params; the cases it can't see (a placeholder callback arg sitting before a used one) rely on this rule.

## Workflow Rules

- **Only write code when the user explicitly asks for it.** Default to analysis, summaries, options, and design. A request to assess, review, summarize, verify, or design something is **not** authorization to implement it — do not write or edit source, migrations, config, or new files, and do not create a plan-shaped code dump, unless the user explicitly says to build/implement/write/fix/change it. When implementation seems like the natural next step, stop and offer it; let the user say yes. (This rule is about _code_; keep updating docs/backlog/PRDs as the task calls for.)
- **Never run `git commit`.** Only humans commit. The LLM may stage files, write code, and run tests, but must not create commits.
- **Always flag warnings and problems — don't silently absorb them.** Any vulnerability discovered (e.g. from `npm audit`), lint/type warning, failing test, or other problem encountered while working must be surfaced to the user. Log every discovered vulnerability as an item in `docs/product-backlog.md` (Engineering section) so it isn't lost, then continue. Never quietly work around or ignore a warning.

Zoom stops at native resolution `ReceiptImageViewer.svelte` fits the image to the viewport at 100% (`handleImageLoad`, `:72`) and caps at a flat `MAX_ZOOM = 400` (`:56`). Those two constants were chosen independently and disagree: a 2400×1000 receipt on a 1440px-tall laptop fits at ~1150px, so 100% is ~48% of native and 400% asks the browser to paint ~4800px from a 2400px file. Everything past roughly 210% is interpolation. On a phone the same 400% lands near 1:1, so the current constant is approximately right there and badly wrong on a desktop. `MAX_ZOOM` becomes derived: `100 × naturalWidth / baseWidth`, the zoom at which one image pixel occupies one CSS pixel. `ZOOM_STEP` is 50 and `zoomIn`/`zoomOut` snap to multiples of it (`:127`, `:134`), so the derived ceiling will rarely be a multiple of 50 — the top step must clamp to the ceiling rather than skip past or become unreachable. Where the fit scale is already clamped at 1 (`:78`) — any image at or below viewport size — the ceiling equals `MIN_ZOOM` and both buttons sit permanently disabled. That is the accepted outcome, not an edge case to patch: there are no further real pixels, and the disabled control says so. It affects small PNGs and low-resolution receipts uploaded before resizing existed. ### 5. Delete `/admin/resize-images` A one-off migration page (~260 lines) whose job is finished. It would now do active harm — it re-resizes at its own hardcoded constants, permanently destroying the extra detail in pre-`901b670` full-resolution originals that the native-resolution zoom ceiling is designed to exploit. It is also the unauthenticated delete-and-reupload route recorded as **M2** in the [backlog](../product-backlog.md); deleting it closes the finding outright. Removing it also removes the second caller of `resizeImage`, so the new constants have exactly one call site. ### No backfill Storage will hold three generations of Receipt Image — full-resolution from before `901b670`, 2000px since, 2400px after this change. Moving validation after the resize changed that calculus: a size rejection thrown inside `withRetry` would be retried three times with backoff, so the person waits ~2.8 seconds per file for a verdict that could not change. I read the full diff, both new spec files, the rewritten specs, the production code, `vite.config.ts`, and the design doc's own test plan — and I ran both projects (server: 38 passed; client/chromium: 10 passed).

## Verdict per file

| File | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `src/lib/utils/imageZoom.spec.ts` | **Solid.** Real, fixed expectations; every branch has a killing mutation. |
| `src/lib/components/ReceiptImageViewer.svelte.spec.ts` | **Genuinely fixed.** Drives the real component; the 1:1 assertion is load-bearing. Two gaps. |
| `src/lib/services/ReceiptService.uploadValidation.spec.ts` | **Mostly real** (ordering/guard tests kill real mutations), but one test asserts its own mock, and three behaviours the diff introduces are unasserted. |
| `src/lib/utils/imageResize.spec.ts` | **Weakest.** The central behaviour of the whole diff — transcode to JPEG — executes in zero tests. |

---

## Findings, most severe first

### 1. `resizeImage`'s body never executes in any test — the transcode is entirely unverified
`/Users/marklevison/Documents/GitHub/YFL/yfl-personal-expense-tracker/src/lib/utils/imageResize.spec.ts:132`

`vite.config.ts` routes `*.svelte.spec.ts` to the Chromium project and *everything else* to node. `imageResize.spec.ts` is not `.svelte.spec.ts`, so it runs in node, where `createImageBitmap` and `document` are both `undefined` (verified: `node -e` prints `undefined undefined`). The three `resizeImage` tests therefore only ever reach the `isResizableImage` early return or the first line after it. Nothing else in the repo calls the real `resizeImage` — every `ReceiptService` spec mocks it.

Mutations that break the feature and break **no test anywhere**:
- `const OUTPUT_TYPE = 'image/png'` (HEIC/PNG no longer become JPEG — the headline change)
- `IMAGE_QUALITY = 0.2` or `1.0`
- `ctx.drawImage(bitmap, 0, 0, bitmap.width, bitmap.height)` — ignore `calculateResizeDimensions` entirely
- drop `toJpegFilename(file.name)` from the returned `new File(...)`
- drop `{ imageOrientation: 'from-image' }` (the EXIF claim at `imageResize.ts:113`)
- drop both `bitmap.close()` calls (the memory fix the design doc calls "a correctness prerequisite")

The design doc's own test plan promises exactly this coverage — `docs/plans/2026-08-03-receipt-image-resize-design.md:185-186`: *"HEIC and PNG both produce `image/jpeg`; output is never larger than the input."* Neither assertion exists.

**Fix:** add `src/lib/utils/imageResize.svelte.spec.ts` — the `.svelte.spec.ts` suffix is the repo's existing route into Chromium for a non-component module (precedent: `src/lib/services/CSVExportService.svelte.spec.ts`). Paint a real 3000×2000 PNG via a canvas → `toBlob` → `File`, then assert on the result of `resizeImage`: `result.type === 'image/jpeg'`, `result.name.endsWith('.jpg')`, `result.size < source.size`, and — decoding the result with `createImageBitmap` — `Math.max(w, h) === 2400` with the aspect ratio preserved. That single test kills all six mutations above.

### 2. `imageResize.spec.ts:145` passes for the wrong reason
`/Users/marklevison/Documents/GitHub/YFL/yfl-personal-expense-tracker/src/lib/utils/imageResize.spec.ts:149`

`await expect(resizeImage(heicFile)).rejects.toThrow()` is green because node throws `createImageBitmap is not a function`, not because HEIC was attempted. It cannot distinguish "tried to decode" from "threw for any reason at all": insert `throw new Error('nope')` immediately after the `isResizableImage` check and it still passes. It does kill one mutation (removing `'image/heic'` from `ACCEPTED_IMAGE_TYPES` makes it resolve), but the test's stated behaviour — "attempts the decode" — is not what's asserted.

**Assert instead:** `vi.stubGlobal('createImageBitmap', vi.fn().mockRejectedValue(new Error('undecodable')))`, then assert the spy was called with `(heicFile, { imageOrientation: 'from-image' })`. That pins both the attempt and the EXIF option.

### 3. `uploadValidation.spec.ts:161` asserts a value the test's own mock supplied
`/Users/marklevison/Documents/GitHub/YFL/yfl-personal-expense-tracker/src/lib/services/ReceiptService.uploadValidation.spec.ts:161`

`stubSuccessfulUpload` (line 75-77) makes `resizeImage` return a file explicitly typed `'image/jpeg'`. So `expect(body.mimeType).toBe('image/jpeg')` is true by construction of the stub. The test does kill one real mutation (reverting `extractReceiptDataFailSoft(path, prepared.file.type)` back to `file.type`), so it isn't worthless — but its name, *"sends the transcoded JPEG type"*, overclaims: nothing in the suite establishes that a HEIC ever becomes a JPEG.

**Assert instead:** tie it to the file actually handed to storage rather than to a literal —
`expect(body.mimeType).toBe((upload.mock.calls[0][1] as File).type)` — and rename to "sends the type of the file we uploaded, not the one the person picked". The transcode itself belongs in finding 1's browser spec.

### 4. The 5MB stored-image limit on the normal (transcoded) path has no test
`/Users/marklevison/Documents/GitHub/YFL/yfl-personal-expense-tracker/src/lib/services/ReceiptService.uploadValidation.spec.ts:82`

`validateReceiptImage` has three outcome branches (`ReceiptService.ts:212-228`). The suite covers `stored-as-received` (PDF, line 139) and `shrink-failed` (line 119). **No test ever produces a `transcoded` result over 5MB.** Mutation: `case 'transcoded': return { ok: true };` — all 7 tests still pass, and the 5MB stored-image contract that ADR-0006 is built around is unenforced.
